summary: Iteration 112 review (Letter-from-Duplicate + Notification Settings). Frontend fully passes: /settings/notifications renders 4 sections with all required data-testids (4 freq radios, 3 channel toggles, 12 topic buttons, targeted toggle, back link), each interaction PATCHes /api/lca1/preferences and shows the 'Saved' indicator. LCA1AlertsBell gear icon (lca1-alerts-settings-link) reliably navigates to /settings/notifications. Preferences GET/PATCH APIs behave as spec'd (defaults merge, 422 on bad frequency). However, POST /api/sd3/candidates/{id}/draft-letter has a FLAKY line-item resolution bug that causes acceptance test test_draft_letter_from_candidate_creates_lf1_and_is_idempotent to fail intermittently (~60-80% of runs). Root cause identified in /app/backend/routes/sd3.py::create_pair.

critical.issue:
In create_pair(), statements a and b are fetched using the original payload order but `ids_sorted = sorted([a_id,b_id])` is used when writing statement_a_id/statement_b_id on the pair doc. Duplicate candidates are then generated from (a,b) in payload order, so candidate.statement_a_line_id refers to whichever statement had the original payload's a-position — which may actually be stored as the pair's statement_b. In draft-letter, we re-fetch statements by pair.statement_a_id / pair.statement_b_id (sorted order) and try _line_by_id — the line often lives in the OTHER statement, so lookup returns {} and the letter content shows 'line item — $? on an unknown date' instead of the real description/amount/date. This is UUID-order dependent, hence flaky. Repro: 3-of-5 runs failed with `assert 'Personal Care Support' in letter['content_draft']`. Fix: fetch a,b using ids_sorted order (or store the pair with the original payload order), so line_ids align. Suggested one-line fix inside create_pair after computing ids_sorted:
    a = await _db.statements.find_one({'id': ids_sorted[0]}, {'_id': 0})
    b = await _db.statements.find_one({'id': ids_sorted[1]}, {'_id': 0})

action_items: Fix SD-3 create_pair statement ordering so that duplicate_candidate.statement_a_line_id / statement_b_line_id align with the sorted statement_a_id / statement_b_id stored on the pair. Simplest fix: re-fetch a,b using ids_sorted before calling _detect_duplicate_candidates(a,b) (and _ai_detect_duplicates).
critical_code_review_comments: SD-3 create_pair sort/detection ordering mismatch (see backend_issues.critical) — causes draft-letter prefill to intermittently omit line item description/amount/date.
draft_letter response returns provider_name only in the create branch; idempotent branch omits provider_name field. Minor consistency issue — main-agent's spec says it should be returned in both.
content_draft template hardcodes 'Mum' fallback for participants without preferred/first name — fine for now but consider referencing participant.name.
seed_data_creation: None; used test's own seeded statements. Cleanup by test fixture works.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Full pytest across core1/loop1/lca1 = 60 passed 3 skipped when run as a suite (flake hid). Run backend/tests/lca1/test_iteration_112.py in isolation 5+ times to catch the flake. Frontend notification settings + gear-link flows are verified.
rca of the issue: In /app/backend/routes/sd3.py create_pair (~line 251-268): a=find_one(payload.statement_a_id); b=find_one(payload.statement_b_id); ids_sorted=sorted([...]); pair stores statement_a_id=ids_sorted[0], statement_b_id=ids_sorted[1]; but _detect_duplicate_candidates(a,b) uses the payload-ordered a,b to compute a_line_id/b_line_id. When payload.statement_a_id > payload.statement_b_id lexically, the pair's stored statement_a corresponds to what was passed as b — so candidate.statement_a_line_id points to a line that lives in pair.statement_b, and vice versa. draft_letter_from_candidate then does _line_by_id(stmt_a_from_pair, cand.statement_a_line_id) → returns None. Prefill becomes 'line item — $? on an unknown date'. Mitigation: after ids_sorted computed, fetch a=find_one(ids_sorted[0]) and b=find_one(ids_sorted[1]) before detection. Reproduction: run pytest backend/tests/lca1/test_iteration_112.py::test_draft_letter_from_candidate_creates_lf1_and_is_idempotent 5 times — 3-4 will fail.
